newsitem.title: USA: Dollar closes up in US, PPI gives slight pause.
newsitem.headline: Dollar closes up in US, PPI gives slight pause.

text.p: The dollar closed slightly higher against the mark and yen but consolidated recent gains after United States inflation data tempered forecasts of an interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve.

Speculation the Fed would signal unease with the economy's inflationary potential later this month helped fuel the six-day dollar rally. But tame producer price data on Thursday may have eroded confidence in such expectations.
"From here, there are still questions about Fed policy, despite fairly widspread expectations of a rate hike," said Bob Lynch, senior currency analyst MMS International.
"Today's PPI data don't necessarily signal any real problem with inflation," he said.
The dollar closed at 1.5125/30 marks, up slightly from 1.5121/24 at the open and 110.13/18 yen, up from 110.05/15.
August producer prices rose a surprising 0.3 percent. But the important "core" component of inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, fell 0.1 percent.
Economists polled by Reuters expected both overall prices and the core rate to rise 0.1 percent.

The dollar crawled to 1.5157 marks in U.S. trade -- Just above Wednesday's 1.5155 mark peak and its highest price since July 16 -- after a report showed Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet told French Parliament leaders the dollar had room to appreciate further versus European currencies.
His comments dovetailed somewhat with dollar-favorable remarks earlier Thursday from Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher, who said official German interest rates could fall.

"The Kuehbacher comment did cause the dollar to rally to the 1.5033 mark level overnignt," said Susan Stearns, a director of foreign exchange sales at Bank of Montreal. "But I don't think the Trichet comment has had any material impact."
Traders said large dollar sell orders, reported near 1.5155/60 marks, capped the dollar's advance.
The dollar also faltered amid a general reluctance to carry positions ahead of August U.S. consumer price and retail sales data on Friday.

But strong data tomorrow could benefit the dollar, if traders grow confident again the Fed will nudge the Federal funds target rate up a quarter percent, when its policy-making arm meets on September 24.

"It's bouncing around, not really with a lot of of direction," said Bill Bertha, chief foreign exchange dealer at Mellon Bank in Pittsburgh. "I think CPI tomorrow will probably be up a bit and that will maybe push it higher again."
Wall Street economists expect August consumer prices to advance 0.2 percent, with an identical rise expected in the core rate.
They forecast a 0.7 percent increase in retail sales.
If the Fed does push the rate up to 5.5 percent this month, it would reverse a 14-month string of three cuts, the last of which was on January 31.
In other trade, the dollar rose to 1.2377/84 Swiss francs from 1.2345/55 Swiss at the open and to Canadian $1.3716/21 from C$1.3715/20.
The pound was at $1.5551/58, up from $1.5545/55 and the Australian dollar fell to $0.7968/73 from $0.7984/89.
-- Alden Bentley 212 859 1667
